articles.title: Linkup /research is async. Treating it as synchronous is the bug, in code and in the freeze case
articles.excerpt: If you ship agents, you have made this mistake: you called an async endpoint, got a pending status back, and then either blocked waiting for a result that was never coming on that call, or polled so h…
articles.body: If you ship agents, you have made this mistake: you called an async endpoint, got a pending status back, and then either blocked waiting for a result that was never coming on that call, or polled so hard you got rate-limited. Linkup's /research works like this, from the docs and the corpus skill. POST /v1/research returns immediately with an id and status pending. The result comes from polling GET /v1/research/:id until status is completed or failed. The recipe is specific: start with a 2 second interval, double it with exponential backoff up to a 10 second cap, and never go faster than 1 request per second, because above that you get rate-limited. Expected wall times: S depth 2 to 5 minutes, M 3 to 7, L 5 to 10, XL 10 to 20.

articles.title: Quentin Tarantino's Near-Perfect New Netflix Thriller Could Be the Next 'Knives Out'
articles.excerpt: The uncanny mix of Quentin Tarantino and David Fincher's unique styles combines to create something new, imperfect, and extremely exciting
articles.body: The story behind The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth isn't quite as dramatic, but the ultimate effect is similar. Nobody died. Quentin Tarantino just made the bizarre decision that his 10th film should be his last and that a sequel to Once Upon a Time in Hollywood wasn't going to cut it. So instead of trashing the film like he did with his last failed effort , Tarantino handed the script off to David Fincher. The result is another unusual melding of directorial styles that doesn't always work (it's definitely not the best either Fincher or Tarantino has to offer), but still manages to provide a uniquely fun time at the movies — and also on Netflix later this year.

articles.title: The Encoded PSEMHUB Path That Broke CVE-2026-35273 WAF Defenses
articles.excerpt: The Encoded PSEMHUB Path That Broke CVE-2026-35273 WAF Defenses The renewed ShinyHunters campaign against CVE-2026-35273 showed how a control can look correct in a policy and fail in production. Mandi…
articles.body: The Encoded PSEMHUB Path That Broke CVE-2026-35273 WAF Defenses The renewed ShinyHunters campaign against CVE-2026-35273 showed how a control can look correct in a policy and fail in production. Mandiant observed requests with /%50SEMHUB/ instead of /PSEMHUB/ . The encoded character reached the vulnerable PeopleSoft servlet while string-based WAF rules missed the path. This detail matters beyond one attack signature. Web application firewalls often inspect the request target before the application performs its own decoding. A mismatch between those two views creates a bypass opportunity. Vulnerability overview CVE-2026-35273 affects Oracle PeopleSoft Enterprise PeopleTools 8.61 and 8.62.

Nod is designed to run on a user's own computer, with local deployment options for macOS and Windows as well as self-hosted setups. The project is licensed under Apache 2.0, making its code available for inspection, modification, and deployment by users and developers. articles.excerpt: The moon shines with Saturn in the constellation Pisces after sunset on Nov. 20
articles.body: The moon shines close to the ringed giant Saturn after sunset on Nov. 20, presenting a spectacular naked-eye display as the stars of the Great Square of Pegasus twinkle nearby. Saturn's steady light will appear a little over 5 degrees from the 82%-lit moon in the southeastern sky after the sun dips below the horizon for viewers in the U.S. — roughly the width of your three middle fingers held at arm's length. Moonlight will hide fainter stars from view, though you should be able to spot Algenib, Markab, Alpheratz and Scheat arrayed in a diamond formation above the lunar disk, marking out the asterism of the Great Square of Pegasus in the November sky.

articles.excerpt: 'They haven’t traveled 24 trillion miles to negotiate. They are coming to exterminate us.'
articles.body: " 3 Body Problem ," Netflix's unsettling adaptation of the first book in Chinese author Cixin Liu's epic alien invasion trilogy, "Remembrance of Earth’s Past," made a serious impact on viewers searching for hardcore E.T. drama and now an explosive new trailer for season 2 has just entered our orbit. This sensational saga about a malevolent interstellar society trying to exist within the unpredictable orbital mechanics of a planet and its triple sun system that forms an Earth-bound armada still has us a bit slack-jawed more than two years after debuting in 2024 . Now we're admittedly eager for this shortened 6-episode sophomore outing, which is officially arriving on Jan. 14, 2027. articles.title: NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars
articles.excerpt: Open data from NASA’s Fermi mission helped an international team of scientists develop a method for finding pulsars about a million times faster than before.
articles.body: 5 min read NASA Science Data Powers New Method to Discover Hard-to-Find Pulsars NASA’s Fermi Gamma-ray Space Telescope, illustrated here, scans the entire sky every three hours as it orbits Earth. Its publicly available data helps scientists find the rapidly spinning cores of dead stars, known as pulsars. NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center/Chris Smith (USRA/GESTAR) An international team of scientists has developed a method that can find pulsars in publicly available NASA data about a million times faster than before. This opens the door to discovering many more of these rapidly spinning objects. A paper describing the results published Thursday in the Physical Review Letters.
